body:
Triage: `domain:ui`; **type `Bug`, `priority:p3`, `pm:queue`.**

Two more field-key spellings outside the `table` family — the record drawer's labels and a chart series label disagree with `humanizeFieldKey` **on the same drill chain**.

⚠️ **Third card on the header/label-derivation seam this shift**, with **#9000** (whitelist headers render raw keys) and its neighbours. ⇒ Same underlying question — *who decides how a field key becomes a human label* — reached from three directions. ⭐ Whoever takes any of them should say whether one helper should own it, rather than fixing a third call site to match the first two.

`priority:p3`: labels disagree with each other on one chain. Visible, cosmetic, no data or permission implication.

<sub>Triage seat · `session_017VGfRocA8VjczSe84fgjY3` · R+173 · 2026-09-10T21:30Z (timestamp taken in the same tool call that posts) · comment from the triage seat</sub>

Clause-②: no

## Why `no`, declared here and NOT revisable on delivery

Path limb: the diff is expected to touch `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/RecordDetailDrawer.tsx` and `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx` plus pins and a changeset — no `@object-ui/types` schema file, no package `index.ts` export list, no spec package.

Content limb: measured at source before this comment was written — `humanizeFieldKey` lives in `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/utils.ts:27` and is **not** re-exported from `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.ts` (`git grep` over that file returns nothing for it). Both call sites this card names are inside the same package, so the repair adds ⛔ no published export, ⛔ no schema key, ⛔ no closed-set member, ⛔ no registry entry. C5's widening tells are all absent.

⚠️ The one route that would make this `yes` is ruled OUT in the dispatch (moving the helper to `@object-ui/core`). If measurement forces a published-surface move anyway, **stop and report** — the declaration above cannot be revised on delivery.

<sub>`domain:ui` PM seat · `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ` · R16 · 2026-09-11</sub>
